CYTOGENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted location] Medical Center
Department of Medical Genetics

PATIENT INFORMATION
Patient Name: [redacted name]
Date of Birth: Not applicable (prenatal)
Medical Record Number: [redacted ID]
Specimen Type: Chorionic villi
Date Collected: [redacted date]
Date Received: [redacted date]
Date Reported: [redacted date]
Referring Physician: Dr. [redacted name]

CLINICAL INDICATION
Prenatal evaluation for potential structural chromosomal abnormality in fetus. Mother is a known carrier of a balanced reciprocal translocation between chromosome 1p and 5q.

FAMILY HISTORY
Mother: Balanced reciprocal translocation carrier t(1;5)(p36.33;q35.3)
Previous pregnancy losses: Not specified

TEST PERFORMED
Interphase Fluorescence In Situ Hybridization (FISH) Analysis

METHODOLOGY
Interphase FISH was performed on uncultured chorionic villi using commercially available subtelomeric probes:
- TeloChromo-1p (1p36.33) - SpectrumOrange
- TeloChromo-5p (5p15.33) - SpectrumGreen
- TeloChromo-5q (5q35.3) - SpectrumAqua

A minimum of 100 interphase nuclei were analyzed for each probe set. The analysis was performed according to standard laboratory protocols and ACMG guidelines.

RESULTS
FISH Result: nuc ish 1p36.33(TeloChromo-1px2),5p15.33(TeloChromo-5px2),5q35.3(TeloChromo-5qx2)

Interpretation: Normal or balanced complement for chromosomes 1 and 5

Cell Count Summary:
- 1p36.33: 98/100 cells with 2 signals
- 5p15.33: 99/100 cells with 2 signals
- 5q35.3: 98/100 cells with 2 signals

INTERPRETATION
The FISH analysis demonstrates two signals for each of the subtelomeric regions tested (1p36.33, 5p15.33, and 5q35.3), indicating either a normal chromosomal complement or a balanced rearrangement for chromosomes 1 and 5. This technique cannot distinguish between a normal karyotype and a balanced translocation inherited from the mother.

The presence of two signals for each region indicates that there is no detectable deletion or duplication of the terminal regions of chromosomes 1p, 5p, or 5q. If the fetus has inherited the maternal balanced translocation, it would be expected to have a normal phenotype, as balanced translocations typically do not result in gain or loss of genetic material.

ADDITIONAL INFORMATION
Previous prenatal testing by PCR demonstrated a normal complement for chromosomes 13, 18, and 21, ruling out the common autosomal trisomies.

RECOMMENDATIONS
1. No further chromosome analysis is indicated at this time based on these results.
2. Genetic counseling is recommended for the parents regarding:
   - The implications of this result
   - The possibility that the fetus may be a balanced translocation carrier
   - Future reproductive risks
3. If the child inherits the balanced translocation, genetic counseling will be recommended at reproductive age to discuss potential risks for future pregnancies.

LIMITATIONS
This FISH analysis is limited to the detection of copy number changes in the specific chromosomal regions tested. It cannot detect balanced rearrangements, point mutations, or abnormalities in other chromosomal regions not covered by the probes used.
